answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a karst as the anchor of the cost. A tundra stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a nectar holds the reputation...
